statement_summary: Maintain a documented security program
Owner designated Security Officer and Privacy Officer in writing
Annual risk analysis using SP 800-30, and after a new PMS or vendor
Risk decision rules; High risks and patient safety risks above Low never accepted as they are
Annual evaluation with an outside review at least every second year
Annual policy review
Sanctions for the relief pharmacist and any future workforce
Confidentiality and security clause in the relief pharmacist's contract
Written, time-limited exceptions
No BAA, no PHI
Annual review of the PMS vendor's SOC 2 report and its customer controls
Keep and read each EPCS certification report before relying on it
Stop EPCS processing when the vendor reports non-compliance
Attended vendor remote support only; sessions logged
Own accounts on every system; no shared or written passwords
MFA on every PHI service, including the PMS administrator role in the store
Unique 14-character passphrases in a password manager
Named people and roles for controlled substance dispensing; license check, same-day removal, quarterly review
Device lock (desktop 3 minutes) and 15-minute PMS timeout
Sealed emergency access codes held by the owner's attorney
Daily EPCS audit report review; monthly PMS and email sign-in review
Only the owner uses the CSOS key, kept under the owner's own account and never copied
Three-level data classification
Restricted data only in approved systems with a BAA
Full-disk encryption on every device
No PHI by ordinary text or email; reminders say only that a prescription is ready
Delete downloaded reports; no patient list exports on devices
Copy local data before device changes; printed master formulation binder
Shredding; device wipe or certified destruction with a record
Six-year retention of security documentation; controlled substance records at least 2 years
Pharmacy devices for pharmacy work only
Updates and antivirus on; standard desktop accounts
Pharmacy network separate from customer Wi-Fi and the camera recorder
No PHI in AI tools without assessment, BAA, and approval; no AI for compounding calculations
regulatory_driver: C-HPH-R01 (164.308(b)(1)); N62-R07 (45 CFR 92.210, parent vertical ID)

statement_summary: Annual security training for both pharmacists
Incident runbook with printed contacts
Same-day incident log with discovery time; relief pharmacist reports the same day
DEA EPCS report within one business day
CSOS key compromise reported within 24 hours
Meet notification deadlines in the P08 matrix
No ransom without counsel and an OFAC check; annual walkthrough
Paper downtime kit with a weekly printed medication list
Transfer arrangement with a nearby pharmacy; relief coverage plan
Controlled substance dispensing, PDMP reporting, and duplicate checks during a PMS outage
